statement: The function $f$ is odd, meaning $f(-x) = -f(x)$ for every real number $x$, and $f(3) = -7$. The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = f(x) + 4$. What is the value of $g(-3)$?

choices.misconception: I mixed up odd and even and thought $f(-3) = f(3) = -7$, so I got $-7 + 4 = -3$.
I assumed $g$ is also odd, so I found $g(3) = -3$ and said $g(-3) = 3$, but adding $4$ breaks the odd symmetry.
I found $f(-3) = 7$ correctly but forgot to add the $4$ in the definition of $g$.

hints: Use the definition of odd to find $f(-3)$ first.
